title: Takeoff Minimums: Legal vs Smart
hook: Zero-zero fog. Can you legally take off? ...Should you?

scenes.narration: Dawn at your home field. Fog so thick the taxiway lights have halos — a quarter mile, maybe less. You're Part ninety-one, flying yourself. The runway's right there, kid.
Quarter-mile fog, Part ninety-one. Is that takeoff LEGAL — yes or no? Commit.
Legal. Part ninety-one has NO required takeoff minimums — zero-zero is technically legal. Why? The F A A regulates hardest where paying passengers sit. Flying yourself, you're free to be dumb alone.
The commercial standard in ninety-one one seventy-five f: one mile with one or two engines, a half mile with more. Published departure minimums on the plate can change those numbers.

The smart number: whatever you'd need to come BACK and land. Engine trouble at three hundred feet in that fog has no chapter in the A I M. Zero-zero is legal the way a fourth espresso is legal — nothing good follows.
Eyes off the screen. The three numbers: legal, standard, smart. Out loud.
Legal: zero-zero. Standard: one mile or a half. Smart: enough to get back in. Fly the third number, kid.
From the alternates lesson — quarter-mile fog at home means your ALTERNATE thinking matters. The three numbers of the one-two-three rule. Again. Go.
Ninety-one one seventy-five, paragraph f. Then go write down your own numbers.

quiz.question: Quarter-mile fog at dawn, Part 91 personal flight. Required takeoff minimums are:
choices: None — but that doesn't make it wise
quiz.explanation: 91.175(f) applies to operators under Parts 121/125/129/135. Part 91 has no takeoff minimums — judgment is the only limit.

quiz.question: Standard takeoff minimums for a commercial operator with 2 engines:
quiz.explanation: Standard: 1 SM for aircraft with two engines or less, ½ SM for more than two. (91.175(f)(1)-(2))

quiz.question: A smart personal takeoff minimum for single-pilot IFR is weather good enough to:
choices: Return and fly an approach back into your departure airport
See the end of the runway
quiz.explanation: If trouble hits right after takeoff, your departure airport is the nearest runway — keep enough weather to use it.
